cli_surface.desktop_discovery: not documented as a stable public endpoint

disposable_unix_transport_attempt.interpretation: This was a transport experiment against a separately launched app-server, not the Desktop process. It proves the Windows proxy/WebSocket transport and provider lifecycle up to turn/start; it is not evidence that the Desktop process exposes an attach endpoint. The model turn remained running at the bounded probe end and the disposable process was then stopped.

desktop_originated_thread_public_endpoin.interpretation: A documented public Unix app-server endpoint, launched separately from the Desktop stdio process but using the same Codex state, listed and resumed an existing thread whose originator was Codex Desktop. A bounded probe sent a no-file-mutation prompt and observed the exact probe response and turn/completed. This proves explicit attach of a Desktop-originated thread through a user-supplied public endpoint; it does not claim that the Desktop stdio process itself exposes a socket or that its UI process was the executor.

tsunagou_a2a_wake_through_desktop_origin.reason_terminal_not_observed: The persisted Desktop thread referenced stale host MCP server paths; app-server kept the turn running after reporting missing tool output. Tsunagou retained running state and did not fabricate turn_completed.
tsunagou_a2a_wake_through_desktop_origin.interpretation: The real Tsunagou daemon accepted an A2A message for an explicitly attached Desktop-originated thread and produced the expected resume/start evidence through the documented public endpoint. Completion depends on the attached thread's own MCP/plugin environment and approval state; this probe therefore proves wake dispatch, not universal Desktop turn completion.

current_desktop_observation.process_owned_loopback_ports: observed but did not accept the documented app-server WebSocket handshake; no endpoint identity inferred
current_desktop_observation.reason: the running Desktop app-server is launched with stdio by the Desktop host; a separate documented app-server listener can nevertheless expose the persisted Desktop-originated thread when the user explicitly supplies that endpoint

verification.unit_tests: uv run pytest -q tests/unit/test_hostwake.py: passed (20 host-wake tests)
verification.python_lint: uv run ruff check src/tsunagou/hostwake tests/unit/test_hostwake.py: passed
verification.disposable_unix_transport: initialize -> thread/start -> thread/read -> thread/resume -> turn/start observed; terminal turn event not observed within bounded probe

conclusion: A manually created Codex Desktop conversation is attachable and wakeable when the user supplies a documented local app-server endpoint and the existing thread id. The running Desktop stdio process still has no public socket and is not inferred through private IPC; without the explicit endpoint, keep durable inbox pull and managed app-server phase A available.
